timeline.title: A Short History of Valentine's Day
items: Chaucer's birds
The poet Geoffrey Chaucer wrote of birds choosing their mates on Saint Valentine's Day. Romance took flight.
A letter from the Tower
Held prisoner in London, Charles, Duke of Orléans, wrote valentine poems to his wife far away in France.
Love by post
A cheap new postal service in Britain meant almost anyone could send a valentine, and the idea took off.
Lace and ribbons
Esther Howland began making lacy valentine cards in America, and the fashion spread far and wide.
today: Not in any history book yet. But ask {from}, and it is the best love story there is.

facts.title: The Science of Being Smitten
items: spark
Butterflies are real
That fluttery feeling is adrenaline at work, sending blood away from your tummy.
pulse
The happy chemical
Love lights up the brain's reward system and floods it with dopamine, the feel good chemical.
book
Dear Juliet
Thousands of letters addressed to Juliet arrive in Verona every year, and volunteers answer them.
heart
Not quite a heart
The classic heart symbol looks nothing like a real heart. Love never worried about accuracy.
leaf
Roses are red
In ancient myths the rose belonged to the goddess of love. It still says I love you today.
smile
Pucker up
A single kiss can use dozens of muscles in the face, and it can help melt stress away.
facts.hand: Science can explain the butterflies. It cannot explain why {who} still gives them to {from}.

note.title: What we believe romance is
paras: We make a lot of magazines, but every now and then one makes us stop and smile. This was one of them.
We believe romance is not only roses and candlelight. It is the text asking if you got home safe, the shared umbrella, the song you both know, the best seat saved just for you.
{who}, someone wanted to tell you something, properly. Not in a card anyone could buy, but in pages full of you: your smile, your habits, the moments that made them fall for you.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, they would choose you over and over again.
note.wish: Happy Valentine's Day, {who}. You are so very loved.
